cards.explanation: The answer is stars. Jesus tells John that the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches (Revelation 1:20). So these words to Ephesus come from the One who holds them in His right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands. I need my whole mustache just to carry ONE cookie box without a wobble, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "I know that you cannot tolerate those who are evil…" Ephesus doesn't put up with them, friends. And He names it right alongside their deeds, their labor and their perseverance (Revelation 2:2).

The answer is that they tested them and exposed them as liars. Jesus says they "…tested and exposed as liars those who falsely claim to be apostles" (Revelation 2:2). Ephesus didn't just nod along, friends. They checked, and the claim didn't hold up. That's a church paying attention.

The answer is Jesus' name. Jesus says they have persevered and endured many things "…for the sake of My name." And He says they did it "Without growing weary…" (Revelation 2:3). I get tired just stamping one batch, friends, so that's a lot to admire.

The answer is that they have abandoned their first love. Jesus says, "But I have this against you: You have abandoned your first love" (Revelation 2:4). Notice He said it right after naming all their good work, friends. The text doesn't say more about what that first love looked like, so I won't guess at it. It's a heavy line, and He says it plainly.

The word is repent. Jesus says, "Repent and perform the deeds you did at first." He also says to keep in mind how far they have fallen (Revelation 2:5). So there's a way back, friends, and He spells it out.

The answer is lampstand. Jesus says, "But if you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place" (Revelation 2:5). Notice the "if" in that warning, friends. Earlier He tells John the seven lampstands are the seven churches (Revelation 1:20), so He's speaking to a church about its own lampstand.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "You hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate" (Revelation 2:6). So Ephesus and Jesus are on the same side here, friends. The text says nothing more about the Nicolaitans in this letter, so that's all I'll say.

The answer is the tree of life. Jesus says, "To the one who overcomes, I will grant the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God" (Revelation 2:7). It's a promise to the one who overcomes, friends. And Jesus says to let the one who has an ear hear what the Spirit says.

The answer is True. Jesus calls Himself "…the First and the Last, who died and returned to life" (Revelation 2:8). He opens the Smyrna letter with those words, friends. And a church facing suffering hears from the One who died and returned to life.

The answer is True. Jesus says He knows their affliction and their poverty, and then adds, "…though you are rich!" (Revelation 2:9). Both are in the same verse, friends. He sees the poverty, and He still calls them rich.

The answer is that Jesus tells them not to fear it. He says, "Do not fear what you are about to suffer" (Revelation 2:10). He doesn't hide that suffering is coming, friends. But He tells them not to fear it.

The answer is to test them. Jesus says the devil is about to throw some of them into prison "…to test you…" (Revelation 2:10). That's the purpose the text gives, friends. It's a heavy part of the letter, and Jesus says it straight.
The word is faithful. Jesus says, "Be faithful even unto death, and I will give you the crown of life" (Revelation 2:10). It's a serious line, friends. And it comes with a promise attached.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death" (Revelation 2:11). It's a promise, friends, and it closes the letter. He says it right after the line about having an ear to hear.
